entries.title: When your child asks for the other parent
entries.summary: Davies describes acknowledging a toddler’s wish for a different parent while the available parent offers care. She also suggests considering recent family changes, without treating one explanation as true for every child.
entries.cue: When your toddler wants one parent for dressing, bathing, reading, or another familiar part of the day.
detail: The parent who is present can put the wish into words and explain that they are helping this time. Davies pairs this clarity with gentleness and understanding.

Travel, a new baby, or moving home are among the changes she suggests considering. A toddler may need extra understanding and closeness; their request does not by itself establish why they feel this way.
Davies acknowledges that repeated preference can feel upsetting or alienating for the other parent. She introduces these ideas as possibilities, with no single approach that fits every family.

qualifications: The book explicitly says there is no single answer for all situations.
Limit testing and wanting control during change are Davies’s proposed interpretations, not established motives.
The child may need additional affection and perspective taking; the book does not require changing caregivers solely for the preference.
